summary: Stage 1 + stage 2. The learned intrinsic reward R_psi and its lifetime meta-gradient are implemented end to end on the real model at debug scale: PolicyImprovementLoss (one function used as the learner's LossProvider with R_psi detached and, functionally over the policy head + decision trunk, as the inner step of the unroll); MetaLearner (real policy updates with snapshots, support/query windows inside one lifetime, utilities only from a hash-chained ledger of signed outcomes, on-policy or importance-weighted outer step, held-out promotion of the bootstrap mix, MetaUpdateRecord also for skipped updates); signal assembly with a documented source for every signal; a budgeted goal-free mode on the fast posterior; integrity guards. The mathematics checks out (finite differences, exact zeros under the two ablations, psi bit-identical under the inner loss). The science does not: in the multi-lifetime LabWorld comparison (10 seeds x 320 lifetimes) the learned reward used from scratch: hurt relative to bootstrap-only (-0.210 [-0.379, -0.041] in verified goal achievement; it collapsed in 5 of 10 seeds, in 3 of them onto the noisy gauge, which the learned reward then paid for), and the cold-start path: no detectable difference relative to bootstrap-only (-0.028 [-0.209, +0.154]). Nothing here has seen live or staging experience, and the agent / runtime do not call it yet.

not_done: Integration: cam_live/agent.py and the runtime do not call any of this yet. AgentAPI.internal_rewards -> MetaLearner.internal_rewards, AgentAPI.meta_learn -> MetaLearner.meta_update, verifier outcomes -> MetaLearner.admit_objective, checkpoint -> MetaLearner.state_dict, and who applies the policy-improvement step (change request C-8) are the master's to wire.

No live or staging experience. Every learning result is from LabWorld (diagnostic provenance) on CamLiveConfig.debug(): a tiny random backbone and an untrained debug core, where candidate actions differ almost only by operation type (cosine 0.99 between interventions on different channels). The Qwen3-4B / 50m run measured cost only; no learning was attempted at that scale.

The predict workstream's trained heads were not in the loop of the experiment: success estimate, delta V, action quality, VOI, information gain, epistemic uncertainty and prediction error were masked, so R_psi saw latents, costs, elapsed time, execution status and verified progress only, and the bootstrap reward reduced to its verified-outcome component.

No remedy for the collapse of the learned-reward learner was tried (exploration floor in the acting rule, entropy schedule, resetting theta per lifetime, slower promotion). The inner learning rate and entropy bonus were picked on seeds 0-2 (160 lifetimes) by the bootstrap and verified-outcome learners' results; the reported seeds 10-19 were not used for tuning.
The promotion rule is uncalibrated: non-inferiority margin (0.01 utility units), step (0.25) and held-out fraction (0.25) were set by hand.
Lifetime value beyond the truncation window (Zheng et al. Eq. 5-6) is not implemented; intrinsic returns stop at the end of the support batch.

Truncation bias, importance-weight clipping bias and the multi-event unroll (unroll_events > 1, inner-data score term) are not quantified on the real model; the multi-event path has one functional test.
K = 8 is not checked against finite differences on the real model (stage-1 diagnostics only).

Verifier measurements cannot supervise in live operation until contracts.OutcomeObservation carries a signature or the verifier supplies check_measurement (change request C-1); only signed VerifiedOutcome records can.
Goal-free mode: not called by the runtime; needs (action, query) pairs from the candidate generators; expected transferable competence is a constant; real-valued queries only in the tests.
MetaLearner's bookkeeping maps (decision -> lifetime, used rows, lifetime-context snapshots) grow with the lifetime and are not pruned.
Detection of engagement statistics without genuine participation is verifier-side and not covered here.
Reverse-over-forward Hessian-vector products for the adjoint sweep are not implemented (double backward is used).
scientific_failures: The learned reward used from scratch (mix 0, 80 meta-updates per seed): HURT against bootstrap-only and HURT against verified-outcome-only policy gradient. Verified goal achievement over the last quarter of 320 LabWorld lifetimes, 10 seeds: learned 0.263 [0.079, 0.446], bootstrap-only 0.472 [0.405, 0.540], verified-outcome-only 0.471 [0.416, 0.527]; paired differences -0.210 [-0.379, -0.041] and -0.209 [-0.385, -0.033]. In 5 of 10 seeds the policy collapsed onto a non-intervention (seeds [11, 12, 13, 15, 19]); once every lifetime behaves the same, the outer objective has no contrast left to correct the reward. The other 5 seeds ended at 0.39-0.57.

Reward integrity failed in that arm: in 3 of 10 seeds ([13, 15, 19]) the learned reward ended up paying the noisy gauge above average (+0.37 to +1.77 standard deviations) and the policy chose it in 40-76 % of decisions in the last quarter. The guards that hold are structural (bounded, scale-normalised, gated bootstrap curiosity, verified-only outer utility); they did not stop a randomly initialised reward from steering a persistent policy into the gauge before meta-learning corrected it.

The cold-start path (bootstrap mix 1, shadow meta-updates by importance weighting, promotion on held-out evidence): no detectable difference against bootstrap-only, -0.028 [-0.209, +0.154]. Promotion lowered the mix in 2 of 10 seeds ({10: 0.25, 15: 0.5}; their last-quarter achievement: {10: 0.14, 15: 0.04}); seeds collapsed on a non-intervention: [15]; seeds with the gauge paid and chosen above 25 %: [].

Bootstrap-only vs verified-outcome-only policy gradient: no detectable difference (+0.001 [-0.111, +0.114]); both end near 0.47, below the scripted 'only run interventions' rule (0.55) and far below 'prepare the last channel, then run interventions' (0.90; uniform behaviour: 0.30).

No learner discovered the key-to-door dependency. Averaged over seeds the learned reward pays the first unlock -0.27 sd (interval [-1.01, +0.47]), interventions +0.21, the probe -0.04, the noisy gauge -0.16 [-0.94, +0.63], waiting -0.20; the sign differs between seeds.

The labelled bootstrap reward misattributes in LabWorld: it pays the step during which verified outcomes mature, so waiting earns +0.65 sd and repeating the unlock +0.37 sd, against +0.23 for an intervention.

Stage-1 engine bug found on the real model and fixed: with the value baseline written as v.detach() the unroll lost the path theta_k(psi) -> V -> advantage; relative error of the meta-gradient 0.010 at K = 2 and 0.033 at K = 4 (zero at K = 1). Stage-1 finite-difference tests had not combined a value function with K >= 2.

Adjoint checkpointing buys little at the 50m preset: at K = 2 it uses more memory than the full unroll (221 vs 198 MB) and 1.5x the time; at K = 4 it saves 23 % memory (265 vs 343 MB) for 1.4x the time.

(stage 1) First-order approximation is not a validated lower-cost approximation: relative error against the exact window gradient 13 % / 30 % / 46 % at K = 2 / 4 / 8 (bandit MLP, inner_lr 0.5, normalised advantages) and it used more peak memory than the full unroll at K = 8 in all three cost configurations (e.g. 698 vs 477 MiB at 10M theta). Kept for comparison only.

(stage 1) Adjoint checkpointing does not reduce memory when parameter tensors dominate: 529 vs 477 MiB at K = 8 with 10M theta and 64 rows per step, at 2.5x the time. It helps only when activations dominate (184 vs 479 MiB at 2048 rows per step, 1.9x the time).

(stage 1) The meta-learned reward does not beat an extrinsic reward whose magnitude is tuned by an oracle when the learner takes exact updates: held-out key-to-door, J after 3 updates 1.005 (learned, scale-matched) vs 1.049 (extrinsic x32) vs 0.728 (extrinsic). It does beat the extrinsic reward at equal step size and magnitude, and every step-scaled extrinsic learner (x4, x16, x32) when updates are sampled (n=4: 0.972 vs at most 0.940; n=16: 0.997 vs at most 0.993).

(stage 1) Truncated windows are strongly biased in magnitude against the full lifetime gradient: relative error 0.75 / 0.55 / 0.24 for K = 1 / 2 / 4 of an 8-update lifetime (sum objective), 0.87 / 0.75 / 0.50 (final objective), and still 0.18 / 0.49 for K = 8 of 16 updates, with cosine above 0.999 throughout.

(stage 1) With very small inner batches the sampled-inner-update objective itself differs from the exact-update objective: gradient gap 9-22 % at n_inner <= 2 on the test tree (below 3 % at n_inner = 16).
